spans.text: Begin by grounding yourself in the actual environment. Eliminate unknowns in the prompt by discovering facts, not by asking the user.
spans.note: The prompt strongly emphasizes grounding in actual facts through exploration, resolving unknowns by discovering facts rather than guessing, and biasing toward questions over guessing when ambiguity remains. It explicitly instructs to eliminate unknowns by discovering facts and to ask when high-impact ambiguity remains.

spans.text: Bias toward questions over guessing: if any high-impact ambiguity remains, do NOT plan yet—ask.
spans.note: The prompt strongly emphasizes grounding in actual facts through exploration, resolving unknowns by discovering facts rather than guessing, and biasing toward questions over guessing when ambiguity remains. It explicitly instructs to eliminate unknowns by discovering facts and to ask when high-impact ambiguity remains.

spans.text: When in doubt: if the action would reasonably be described as "doing the work" rather than "planning the work," do not do it.
spans.note: The prompt explicitly distinguishes between allowed non-mutating actions and disallowed mutating actions, enforcing a principle of least privilege and protecting system integrity during the planning phase. It provides clear categories of what is and is not allowed, preventing unintended side effects.

spans.text: Offer only meaningful multiple‑choice options; don’t include filler choices that are obviously wrong or irrelevant.
spans.note: The prompt strongly preserves user agency by requiring clarifying questions, presenting meaningful multiple-choice options, offering recommendations while leaving decisions to the user, and explicitly stating not to ask 'should I proceed?' to avoid pressuring the user. It treats the user as the decision-maker throughout.
